question: Can the common available catalogue be served through real native retrieval before testing learned furniture policies in complete scenes?
actual: Pinned native retrieval, scoring, size ranking, queue, HTTP endpoints/client and mesh export. Cached vectors supply only three exact descriptions. Full CLIP imports omitted in v2, using two exact original function definitions; all other exercised native retrieval modules imported in full.

policies.available_first: argmin dimension_L1 over topK(similarity(query), C_full intersect C_local)
policies.difference: Filtering after top-K and filtering before top-K are different selection policies. Availability policy changes candidate identities even when both return an asset. It must be fixed and shared across model/search arms.

findings: Bed and nightstand identities changed under available-first; wardrobe became retrievable. No semantic superiority follows from returning a mesh.

All returned metadata lacked up/front. Alignment function executed its no-transform branch. Subsequent VLM orientation/material estimation, Blender conversion, convex collision geometry and SDF construction are still required by native AssetManager.
Native source-size ranking follows CLIP filtering. It can choose a lower CLIP score with a closer bounding-box size. This is the existing retriever, not Agent reasoning.
The old index offset audit was rediscovered and read, not rerun as a new achievement. No hypothetical index remap applied.

nearest_work.bounded_paraphrase: SceneSmith already evaluates an HSSD retrieval ablation, and its retrieved-asset validator is more permissive about appearance and minor structure. Our cache restriction is not an independent new method. Native validation acceptance must remain distinct from original-task semantic satisfaction.

scientific_claim: No new algorithm established. This closes part of the shared execution environment so future effects are not confounded by hidden asset-policy differences.
not_admitted: Unseen text descriptions without actual CLIP inference
Simulation-ready SceneObject without native physics/collision conversion
Asset category/material/count correctness based only on a name or CLIP score
Whole scene success from successful HTTP replies
